Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Keep the supplied language.", "input": "i want to talk through the next maintenance pass on the family photo importer because the last import looked mostly right but left us with a few questions about what happened to the originals. the library belongs to my mother and my aunt and it has pictures from both sides of the family, so please keep the two source folders distinct while describing the changes. the desktop running the importer is called cedar and it is on the home network in the upstairs office. the machine is not a server and it can be switched off overnight. we normally copy new pictures on saturday morning, but the older folders are only checked when someone notices a gap. i want the instructions to fit that actual routine rather than assume a person is watching the screen all day.

archive.retain_originals

new paragraph when the saturday copy is finished, leave a short log on cedar with the date, the source folder name, the number of files copied, and any review items still waiting. my cousin wants to know whether he can safely remove the card, so show a finished message only after the writes have completed and the archive drive is available. if the import is interrupted before that point, say it was interrupted and name the last file that completed, when that information is known. the log should not include a guessed reason for an interruption. we sometimes copy the same card twice because someone finds another envelope of pictures after the first pass, and a later run should be able to recognize files already present without quietly discarding a new version that has different image data. if there is not enough information to make that distinction, hold the files for review.
new paragraph finally, the family will try the revised importer on porch test before we use it on the next saturday card. the test should include the unreadable-file case if we can reproduce it, and we should verify that the archive remains unchanged when a viewing copy is rotated. my aunt will check the folder names, my cousin will check the external drive notice, and i will compare the report against the files that actually landed in the test library. if any of those checks cannot be completed, leave that item open in the report rather than marking it done. the next real import is planned for saturday morning, but only if the archive drive mounts correctly and the test does not show a new problem. until those conditions are met, keep the current importer available for the family's existing library and do not move the original folders.", "output": "I want to talk through the next maintenance pass on the family photo importer because the last import looked mostly right but left us with a few questions about what happened to the originals. The library belongs to my mother and my aunt, and it has pictures from both sides of the family, so please keep the two source folders distinct while describing the changes. The desktop running the importer is called Cedar, and it is on the home network in the upstairs office. The machine is not a server, and it can be switched off overnight. We normally copy new pictures on Saturday morning, but the older folders are only checked when someone notices a gap. I want the instructions to fit that actual routine rather than assume a person is watching the screen all day.

The incoming card folder is called Kitchen Card, and it is usually copied from a card reader into the staging folder before anything is added to the library. Last Saturday there were 184 files in that folder, including 11 short videos and 3 pictures with no date in their camera information. The importer should keep those videos in the same event folder as the still pictures from the card, but it should not pretend that a video date is the date the picture was taken. If the date is missing, leave the file in the review queue and show the filename there. There were two files with the same camera filename, and one came from my aunt's old camera, so a filename by itself cannot be treated as proof that two files are duplicates. We use the camera make and file size as clues, not as a final decision.

Please leave the setting archive.retain_originals enabled when you update the configuration. The key is used on Cedar, and my cousin checks it before he copies a card, so changing its case or moving it to a different setting name would cause confusion. It means the original file stays in the incoming archive after a corrected copy has been created for viewing. We do not want the importer to replace an original just because the viewing copy has a rotation fix. The archive is on an external drive labeled Family Blue, and the drive is connected only during a copy or a restore. If that drive is not mounted, stop before the import starts and show a clear notice; do not silently send the archive to the computer's internal disk. Last month the drive letter changed after a restart, so the check should use the drive label and the configured location together.

archive.retain_originals

Section 1: Checks before copying.
1. Show the source folder and the destination event folder on the same screen.
2. Show how many files are waiting and how many are already in the library for that event.
3. Warn about unreadable files without hiding the filenames.
4. Ask for confirmation before the first file is written, but do not ask separately for every file in the same batch.
5. If the user cancels at that point, leave the card folder and the archive unchanged.

I said five checks, yes, and the unreadable-file warning belongs before confirmation, not after the copy has begun. The screen can be plain, but the button labels need to be clear enough for my aunt to use without calling me.

We have an event folder named Orchard Picnic for the pictures from June 18, 2017. It has 42 images, and a handwritten note says the group picture was taken near the south gate. The importer should not rename that event from the note, because the note is an extra clue and not the official folder title. The image dates were adjusted on 7 files when my aunt scanned printed photographs, and those adjusted dates need to stay as entered. For scans with no embedded camera information, the importer can keep the date that a person entered, but it should label that date as a manual date in the details panel. A scan made this winter should not appear as if it was photographed this winter just because it was added recently. The import date and the photo date are different pieces of information, and both are useful when we look back at how the collection was assembled.

On the first test run, use a copy of the folder called Porch Test and do not point the test at the family's only archive. That test folder has 26 files and 4 subfolders, with one empty subfolder called Receipts. Leave the empty folder alone until we decide whether it is an old filing mistake or a place someone intends to use. I was going to say delete it—no, leave it in place and mention it in the test report. The report should say which files were copied, which ones were skipped, and why each skipped file was held back. If a file fails because it cannot be read, the importer should continue with the other files in the test batch and record the failure, rather than stop after the first problem. If the external drive disconnects during the test, stop the remaining writes and tell the user how many files had already completed. Do not claim that the whole batch succeeded in that situation.

Section 2: Naming and review.
Keep the folder names relatives already recognize, including Aunt May Scans and Grandpa Workshop. Don't convert names to initials, and don't guess a person's identity from a face in a picture. There are 9 folders with the word May in their names, and only one is Aunt May Scans, so a broad search result could be misleading. When two likely matches appear, show both paths and let the user choose whether they belong together. The importer can offer a possible duplicate warning when the image dimensions and file size are the same, but the user still needs to see the comparison before either file is removed or merged. If a caption has been typed by a family member, keep the wording and show who entered it when that information is available. My mother once entered the caption, “The dog got into the picnic again,” and it refers to a specific picture, not every picture from that afternoon. Keep the caption attached to that one image even if the event folder is reorganized.

For the smaller repair, there are 12 rotated scans in Grandpa Workshop, and the thumbnail view currently shows 5 of them sideways. The scan files themselves should stay as they are in the archive; apply the viewing rotation only to the copy used by the library. After the repair, compare the thumbnails with the archive versions and make sure that the repair did not change the original scan. If the software cannot tell whether a rotation is already recorded, put that image in the review queue instead of applying another turn. This matters because one of the scans was rotated by hand before it was uploaded, and a second rotation would put it back on its side. The notes in the folder mention a date of November 3 but do not say whether that is the scan date or the date of the workshop, so do not use it to fill a missing photo date.

When the Saturday copy is finished, leave a short log on Cedar with the date, the source folder name, the number of files copied, and any review items still waiting. My cousin wants to know whether he can safely remove the card, so show a finished message only after the writes have completed and the archive drive is available. If the import is interrupted before that point, say it was interrupted and name the last file that completed, when that information is known. The log should not include a guessed reason for an interruption. We sometimes copy the same card twice because someone finds another envelope of pictures after the first pass, and a later run should be able to recognize files already present without quietly discarding a new version that has different image data. If there is not enough information to make that distinction, hold the files for review.

Finally, the family will try the revised importer on Porch Test before we use it on the next Saturday card. The test should include the unreadable-file case if we can reproduce it, and we should verify that the archive remains unchanged when a viewing copy is rotated. My aunt will check the folder names, my cousin will check the external drive notice, and I will compare the report against the files that actually landed in the test library. If any of those checks cannot be completed, leave that item open in the report rather than marking it done. The next real import is planned for Saturday morning, but only if the archive drive mounts correctly and the test does not show a new problem. Until those conditions are met, keep the current importer available for the family's existing library and do not move the original folders."}]
